claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 15 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex who is 15 and lives with you at home.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in education (such as school)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. And one final question:

**Is Alex in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or does he have any circumstances where he's living away from home for extended periods?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually he has been in local authority care for a bit now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. This is important information. 

**How long has Alex been in local authority care - is it more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been more than 8 weeks - about 12 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. This is an important detail. Let me ask:

**Does Alex spend any regular time at home with you each week - for example, does he come home for at least 24 hours a week, or does he spend at least 2 nights in a row each week at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about the exact amount of time. It varies quite a bit week to week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that it can vary. Let me ask this in a different way to help clarify:

**In a typical week, does Alex come home to stay with you, and if so, roughly how many nights per week does he usually spend at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It really does vary - some weeks he might come home, other weeks he might not. I honestly can't say there's a typical pattern.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. Let me ask one more question that might be relevant to your situation:

**Even though Alex is in care and doesn't come home regularly, do you regularly spend money on him - for example, buying him clothes, presents, giving him pocket money, or contributing financially in other ways?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do spend money on him when I can - buying him clothes, the odd present, that sort of thing.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 15 and in school, which normally meets the age and education criteria
- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex
- However, Alex has been in local authority care for about 12 weeks (more than 8 weeks)

**The key issue:**
When a child has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you can still receive Child Benefit if the child spends **at least 24 hours per week at home** with you. Since Alex's time at home varies significantly from week to week with no consistent pattern, I cannot determine whether he regularly meets this 24-hour threshold.

**My recommendation:**
You should **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** at HMRC. They will be able to:
- Review your specific circumstances in detail
- Look at Alex's actual visiting pattern over recent weeks
- Make a proper determination about your eligibility

They can help you understand whether the time Alex does spend at home is sufficient to maintain your Child Benefit entitlement, or advise you on what you need to do next.
